sn35.133:1.2: It is unusual, if not unique, to see a female brahmin with a student. Below, she is referred to as the “tutor’s wife” (_ācariyabhariyā_); compare Chāndogya Upaniṣad 4.10, where a tutor’s wife (_ācāryajāyā_) discusses the education of the pupil. Now, Verahaccāni is not an attested clan name, and Sanskrit _vairahatya_ means “manslaughter”. Given that her husband is rather mysteriously absent, perhaps _verahaccāni_ is a term for brahmin ladies whose husbands were murdered. Compare _nirvīrā_, a woman whose husband and children are dead.
